label: Prospector Pell's first greeting — the shard re-identification

purpose.value: Pell greets the hero across the assay table and patiently re-identifies his 'dark shards' as what they are: irrigation runes and heating stones taken from someone's home.

emotionalProgression.note: A returning supplier of specimens gets the guild's brisk, friendly verdict-first manner.
He names each shard honestly — heating stone, irrigation rune, maker's mark — and whose it was.
The hero logs 'demon embers' in his journal and thanks him for the appraisal; Pell watches him go like a stone that won't grade.

notes: Misunderstanding pair (Lore.md): he says 'That is an irrigation rune — somebody's tomatoes are dry because of you'; the hero writes 'demon ember' in the journal. Pell KNOWS the book is a children's comedy and may say so; the hero hears a disguise over prophecy. He only suspects the banking mechanism, so fact_banking_uses_diplomatic_network must not be stated by him. Never validate the hero's prophecy framing: there is no canon fact supporting 'the realms are evil', and that absence is itself the guard.
